newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Aid work suspended for second day in east Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Aid work suspended for second day in east Zaire.

text.p: Aid work was suspended for a second straight day on Tuesday because of unrest but workers said they would try to contact three camps holding nearly 90,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees.
"It is a de facto suspension of operations here today but we are working on re-establishing contact with the camps," said Paul Stromberg, a spokesman for the U.N. refugee agency UNHCR.
Zaireans armed with machetes rampaged south of the northeastern Zairean city of Kisangani on Monday against Rwandan Hutu refugees they blamed for killing at least six villagers.
Some Zaireans said they looted vehicles at the urging of the Tutsi-dominated rebels who have seized half of Africa's third largest country since October.
They said aid convoys were carrying arms for the Hutus in bags of maize and they would stop all aid workers from passing. U.N. operations south of Kisangani were suspended.

Stromberg said a commission of representatives of UNHCR, the Rwandan government and the rebel alliance was expected to visit Kisangani on Tuesday and might try to overfly or even visit the camps for 87,000 refugees.
"The last information we received is the refugees remain at their sites," he added.
An estimated 55,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees in poor health are in makeshift camps at Kasese 25 km (15 miles) south of Kisangani and 32,000 more at Biaro, 42 km (25 miles) south of the city.
UNHCR chief Sadako Ogata said on Monday a rebel operation near Kasese camp on Monday following the reported killings of at least six Zaireans had raised fears of a new refugee exodus.
"We are sending no food to the camps today because we want security guarantees for staff," said Michele Quintaglie, spokeswoman for the World Food Programme (WFP), on Tuesday.

"We have lost more than half a million dollars worth of food and supplies from looting over the past few days," she added. She said a new food distribution due in Bairo on Monday was delayed by the unrest.
"We know times are going to be tough in Biaro for the next few days," said Quintaglie, adding camps at Kasese should have enough food for three days.
Residents said armed Hutu refugees attacked a village near Kasese on Monday and killed at least six people. Journalists saw six bodies and local authorities said up to eight Zaireans were killed.
Villagers looted a train with food for Hutu refugees near Lula early on Monday and a WFP warehouse and two railway wagons near Kasese. A total of 191 tonnes of food aid were seized.
Aid workers said they feared the looters, who stopped aid workers reaching camps south of Kisangani on Friday and Monday, were being encouraged by the rebels. Rebels deny any role.
The governor of Zaire's Eastern province, appointed with rebel blessing, said on Sunday a U.N. airlift for the refugees should not start until May 5 due to a cholera epidemic.
Aid officials say fears of cholera were exaggerated. Deaths from cholera, malaria and malnutrition among the refugees stood at about 90 a day on Sunday.

The refugees are the rump of more than two million Hutus who fled Rwanda in 1994 after the victory of Tutsi rebels in the civil war and the genocide of 800,000 Tutsis and Hutu moderates. The refugees have fled 600 km (375 miles) since last October to avoid the Zairean Tutsi-dominated rebels, supported by Rwanda's government.
